purpose: Teach the orientation, support and stop-order rules behind a feasible mixed load.
headline: Three constraints shape the load
subtitle: Check the resting face, the supporting surface and the delivery order.

takeaway: A gap is usable when the unit fits, has support and can be unloaded at the intended stop.
caption: Figure 2. Three constraints shape the load. Allowed orientations set the base, stackability determines what can rest on it, and delivery order determines where each group belongs.
alt_text: Orientation arrows show R1 length, R2 width and R3 height vertical. Two stacks show when a top can support other cargo. A trailer schematic shows A–C at the nose for stop 2, and D–G at the rear doors for stop 1.
source_notes: Orientation and stackability definitions from the Transport service contract. A–C and D–G positions from verified case groups. Zones are schematic; no exact geometry, support rating or verified unloading path is shown.
